transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-28
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Harper (Redwood Solutions), Priya (AscendGrid Head Infra), Omar (AscendGrid Cloud Architect), Sofia (CTO), Daniel (Partner Manager)

Summary: quick partner intro + technical discovery about Dedicated/private deployment on AscendGrid GPUs, initial ask for benchmarks and pilot timeline.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Lucas our SE and Harper who helps partner ops. Could you do quick intros on your side?
00:12 Priya: Sure, hi I'm Priya Nair, head of infra at AscendGrid. We run a GPU cloud focused on enterprise workloads, mix of A100 and H100, some custom interconnects. Daniel's our partner manager, Omar is our cloud architect and Sofia is CTO.
00:27 Maya: Awesome, thanks. Quick call goals - want to understand AscendGrid's partner motion and what a joint integration would look like: Dedicated pools, Private control planes, co-sell, and pilot ops. Also curious about networking and security constraints.
00:45 Daniel: Yeah from partner ops perspective we want to see where Redwood sits in the stack and how tightly we integrate - like do we host Redwood Dedicated on our infra, or do you support a native private deployment where Customer controls everything?
00:58 Lucas: Great question. There are a couple models. For Dedicated you'd reserve capacity on your infra but Redwood runs the inference runtime; for Private we can install a customer-managed control plane in their VPC or on-prem. Both are supported, and there are tradeoffs around telemetry, updates and SLA.
01:18 Omar: When you say install in our VPC, is that a thin control plane or do you ship a full runtime that lives inside our network? Network egress/ingress and KMS access are big concerns for our enterprise customers.
01:30 Harper: It can be either. We typically provide a private control plane that talks to a runtime deployed inside the customer's VPC - keys stay on customer KMS, and audit logs remain in the customer's logging endpoint. For Dedicated on a partner cloud, we'd work with you on network routing and peering - there is some light coordination.
01:50 Priya: Ok. On hardware compatibility - our fleet is mostly A100s, a growing H100 pool, and we have a new accelerator on test. How opinionated is Redwood on kernel/kernels and quantization support? We run a mix of FP16 and int8 workflows.
02:05 Lucas: We support a range of quantization profiles; our runtime picks optimized kernels based on model architecture and sequence length distribution. For int8 we do quantization-friendly execution paths. That said, we like to validate kernels per hardware - that's a big part of the PoC.
02:25 Sofia: Are there any GPUs you don't support or that require extra work?
02:30 Lucas: Very new or proprietary accelerators sometimes need a short porting phase; we can usually get baseline performance within a week or two for common families. We should get your specific models and a small benchmark corpus.
02:42 Omar: Ok we'll share inventory. On the networking front, do you require NAT egress to Redwood endpoints for control plane, or can it be fully air-gapped?
02:53 Harper: For a fully air-gapped private deployment we provide an on-prem package; it's a heavier lift but supported. For VPC deployments we typically require outbound to our control plane for updates/metrics, though sensitive customers can opt to host the control plane entirely.
03:10 Priya: Security: SOC2 is a must for our customers. How does Redwood handle encryption at rest, KMS integration, and SSO?
03:19 Maya: We're SOC2 compliant and integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported and we offer RBAC. We'll send SOC2 docs and a security checklist.
03:30 Daniel: Great. On the business side - what does pricing look like for partner Dedicated capacity? We run reserved capacity deals and want to understand economics - do you do revenue share or fixed fees?
03:42 Maya: We have partner program options. For Dedicated we typically do a reserved capacity contract with a commit and an option for revenue share on co-sell. Terms can be flexible. We'll share a partner one-pager and sample pricing.
03:56 Priya: For pilots, typical ask from our customers is predictable latency under 100ms for small prompts and throughput for batch workloads. Can you share previous benchmarks or run a benchmark against our hardware?
04:08 Lucas: Yes. We'll propose a benchmark plan: prefix caching, batching profiles, and sample prompts. We can instrument per-token latency and cost. It helps if you can provide expected prompt size distribution and sample payloads.
04:22 Omar: We can provide sample workloads. Network topology: we prefer peered VPCs with private routing rather than open peering. How does Redwood handle multi-tenant isolation if we host many customer workloads?
04:36 Lucas: For Dedicated pools we provide tenant isolation via separate runtime instances and namespace-level quotas. KV cache handling is per-tenant. For Private deployments, isolation is under your control. Note: sometimes the transcript mis-heard 'K V cash' in our logs.
04:51 Sofia: Noted. On SLA - what uptime and latency guarantees do you offer for Dedicated?
04:57 Maya: We can offer SLA-backed uptimes and latency targets with dedicated reserved pools. Exact numbers depend on commit and capacity profile; we can propose an SLA in the partner contract.
05:08 Priya: One concern - lifecycle management: model rollouts, version pinning, fallbacks. We need to ensure that if a model degrades we can auto-fallback to a safe variant.
05:18 Lucas: We support versioning and rollout policies including canary and A/B. Automatic fallback to compatible model variants is part of resilience strategies. We also have eval hooks to monitor quality regressions against test prompts.
05:34 Daniel: Sounds good. For go-to-market, we have partners who value co-marketing and joint sales plays. What's Redwood's partner motion?
05:44 Maya: PLG-led self-serve, but partner/dedicated deals are handed to sales. We support co-sell, provide partner enablement, and joint technical resources for proofs-of-concept.
05:57 Priya: Ok next steps?
06:00 Maya: We'll share: partner one-pager, partner terms and initial pricing; Lucas will share a benchmark checklist and pre-PoC questionnaire. AscendGrid to share cluster inventory, network topology, and security contacts. We'll find a date for SE deep-dive week of 2026-03-09.
06:22 Omar: That works. Do you need any sample data for quality testing?
06:25 Lucas: Yes, sample prompts and expected distributions are very helpful. We don't need PII in samples; synthetic or redacted examples are fine.
06:34 Priya: Also want to kick off NDA? For pilots with customers we often need an NDA before sharing more sensitive architecture docs.
06:40 Maya: We can route that through legal - Daniel, send any standard NDA and we'll review.
06:45 Sofia: One last question: what's a realistic timeline from pilot to general availability on partner infra?
06:50 Maya: Pilot start to GA depends on complexity; for a straightforward Dedicated integration we often see a 6-10 week timeline from pilot start to GA if benchmarks and security checks go smoothly. For Private on-prem installs it can be longer.
07:04 Daniel: Ok thanks everyone, that was helpful. We'll get materials over this week.
07:08 Maya: Thanks - we'll follow up with next steps and calendar invite for the SE deep-dive.
07:12 End of call.

Notes on transcription: Some speaker markers and product names may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., K V cache/KV cache, Redwood Dedicated named variations). Refer to action items above.
